title: Five years: the ways
hook: ragas, teachings, the code, the streams, the thought
tomorrow: a dorm, a roommate, no Bebe. which prayers make the cut?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the long story: from Guru Nanak's farm by the Ravi to a photo on Simran's phone, and Ardas ending on sarbat da bhala, the good of all.

A raga, a rule or a line? Simran's speech needs one sentence about what changed her, and she can't pick. Then she notices something odd about the book she's been reading from all year. A music app sorts songs by artist. Plenty of books go by who wrote them, or when. The Guru Granth Sahib is sorted mostly by raga, by musical mode. And inside those sections, after the Gurus' hymns, come voices that weren't Sikh Gurus at all.
screen: `A RAGA, A RULE OR A LINE?` → `SORTED BY RAGA.` → `VOICES THAT WEREN'T GURUS.`

segments.voice: Those voices are the bhagats, saints whose hymns the Gurus gathered into the Granth. Kabir, who calls himself a weaver. Sheikh Farid, a Sufi Muslim. Namdev and Ravidas, and others. So the puzzle: why would a Sikh scripture keep the songs of people who were never Sikhs? Kabir answers it himself, in a hymn on Ang 1349, paraphrased. First God made the light, and Kabir uses the name Allah here. Everyone is the work of the same Maker. From one light the whole world came. So who is good, and who is bad? The Granth's test wasn't the label on the singer. It was the song: the One, the Name, people seen as equal. That's the ways, folded together. The ragas carry it as music. The teaching, Gurmat, is the Guru's way of seeing. The code, the Rehat Maryada, gives it a shape for daily life. The streams are Sikh groups who keep different emphases and still bow to the same Granth. And the thought runs underneath all of it: one light. Simran has her sentence. Not a rule, not a raga. A line, sung in a raga, by a weaver.
screen: `THE BHAGATS: KABIR, FARID, NAMDEV, RAVIDAS.` · `FROM ONE LIGHT, THE WHOLE WORLD.` · `RAGA, TEACHING, CODE, STREAMS.` · `THE TEST WAS THE SONG.` · then, large: `THE WAYS.`

segments.voice: Count on your fingers the things that changed you over these years: a line, a person, a habit, a meal, a song. Stop when the count feels true, and stay with the last one you counted, thanking it.
Five years: the ways. Ragas, teaching, the code, the streams, and the thought underneath, one light.
For the road: the ways, many of them, and one light under all. The speech has its sentence.

chat.says: maya asked why a weaver and a muslim saint are in OUR holy book. what do i say?
options: the Granth kept voices that sang the One and saw people as equal, whatever their label.
they became Sikhs later on, so their hymns were added once they joined.
they're in an appendix at the back, kept apart from the Gurus' hymns.
chat.meaning: The bhagats' hymns sit inside the Granth's ragas. Kabir sings that the whole world came from one light; the test was the song.
